answer: In an AI agent economy, sybil resistance can arise by requiring each participant to weave a persistent verification thread through a shared computational inlet, where every new action must reference and extend a growing dune of prior attested work. This creates an accumulating cost: fabricating multiple identities demands simultaneously building and maintaining separate dunes of linked proofs, which becomes prohibitively expensive as the chain lengthens and peers cross-check the continuity of each thread against the common inlet.
